question: When AI agents can act for us online, who should check that they act safely?
reflection: Rules and oversight can help powerful tools earn trust, so that more people can share their benefits with less fear.

sources.subject: Google Gemini 4 Argon hits 1M output tokens, restricted launch
OpenAI's billion-user race to catch up

one_line: US regulators start looking hard at AI agent safety, while Google and OpenAI release models built for long, unbroken agent work.

top_stories.title: US consumer regulator opens an AI safety inquiry
top_stories.what: The US Federal Trade Commission is reportedly seeking records from OpenAI, Anthropic and the evaluator METR about the risks of agents that browse and act for users.
top_stories.why: Regulators asking how agents behave creates demand for evidence on user trust, consent and harm, which is behavioural research territory.

top_stories.title: Google and OpenAI ship models for long agent tasks
top_stories.what: Google's Gemini 4 Argon can reportedly write up to a million tokens in one answer but is limited to vetted security partners for now, while OpenAI added GPT-6.1 Sol and a paid high-speed tier.
top_stories.why: Longer and faster outputs make it practical to run full document reviews or coding of large qualitative datasets in one pass.

top_stories.title: Building AI needs more skilled trades than exist
top_stories.what: An industry report says the US needs about 1.7 million new tradespeople a year to 2035, while training covers only about half that need.
top_stories.why: Skills gaps behind the AI build-out are a workforce planning question that labour-market agencies can study with real data.

saudi_lens.text: Saudi Arabia is building large data centres too, so the shortage of electricians and cooling technicians is a local planning issue for technical colleges and the labour market.

idea.title: Data-centre trades skills map
idea.pitch: Estimate how many electricians, cooling technicians and mechanics planned data centres will need, and compare that with current training output.
idea.first_step: List announced data-centre projects in the Kingdom and the trades each one typically needs.

idea_kids.title: Build a city power board game
idea_kids.pitch: A board game where children place homes, schools and a data centre on a map and share limited power and workers between them.
idea_kids.first_step: Sketch a simple grid map and make cards for power units and worker types.

terms.definition: An AI system that can take steps on its own, such as browsing, using software or buying things, to finish a task for a person.

concepts.summary: Regulators begin asking who answers for harm when AI agents act for users.
Models built to produce very long outputs so agents can finish big tasks without stopping.
